title: First-PR developer journey outline (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc maps the smallest high-confidence path for a new developer to make their first meaningful contribution (open a PR that changes behavior, adds a tiny example, or fixes docs) across Redwood Inference client libraries and quickstarts. The focus is on reducing cognitive hops: fewer repo setup steps, reproducible local runs, and a short PR checklist that maintainers can review quickly.

Why this is important (hypothesis):
- A lower time-to-first-PR increases contributor retention and helps internal cross-team collaboration.
- For external adopters, a reproducible tiny change builds trust (they can test and iterate).
- Measuring and optimizing this flow will help us prioritize docs vs. infra work (CI flakiness hurts onboarding more than prose).

Success metrics (what to measure):
- Time-to-first-local-run: goal < 20 minutes (from clone to running sample request)
- Time-to-first-PR: goal < 60 minutes for a small change
- PR acceptance rate for first-time contributors: goal > 80% (internal contributors for initial experiment)
- Number of help requests in #dev-x within 24h of clone: target < 1 per dev
- CI flakiness rate on contributor PRs: < 5% failures not related to the PR change

Target personas:
- New engineer on Redwood infra team (familiar with Python/Node, not with our runtime internals)
- Solutions engineer building a customer sample app
- External open-source adopter evaluating client libraries

Pre-reqs (to reduce friction):
- Minimal system deps: Docker + 1 package manager (npm or pip)
- Optional: access token generator script in repo that uses a test key (no manual Console steps)
- A one-command local-run: e.g. `make run-sample` or `yarn start:example`

High-level journey (ideal minimal path):
1) Clone repo and cd in
   - `git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/client-examples.git`
   - `cd client-examples`
2) Start an ephemeral local backend or demo mode
   - `./scripts/start-demo.sh` (spins up a tiny HTTP shim that returns recorded responses)
3) Install deps and run sample
   - `make install` or `npm ci` / `pip install -r requirements-dev.txt`
   - `make run-sample` (opens a tiny sample that sends a request to the demo backend and prints the result)
4) Make a tiny change (docs comment, tweak prompt, add an assertion)
5) Run tests locally (`make test`) and lint (`make lint`)
6) Open PR with template auto-filled for quick review

Concrete artifacts to add/update across repos:
- README top-level: 3-line summary + 1-liner command to run example
- `scripts/start-demo.sh`: deterministic demo backend (no cloud keys)
- `Makefile` targets: install, run-sample, test, lint, format
- PR template: short checklist with `run-sample` and `make test` checked
- GH Actions: dedicated CI path for small contributor PRs that favors speed (cache deps, skip heavy integration tests unless tag present)

First-PR friendly PR checklist (to add to PR template):
- [ ] I ran `make run-sample` and saw the sample output
- [ ] I ran `make test` locally (or CI passes fast checks)
- [ ] My change is < 200 lines (small PR)
- [ ] I updated README or example if behavior changed
- [ ] I added a line to changelog/EXAMPLES.md if needed

Common friction points & mitigations (notes to self):
- Problem: Tokens and Console signup steps block progress
  - Mitigation: include `demo-mode` in clients that uses canned responses; `scripts/generate-test-token.sh` for internal devs only
- Problem: CI is slow/flaky and blocks contributor momentum
  - Mitigation: create a `fast-check` workflow for contributor PRs that runs lint + unit tests only and reports clearly which checks are required for maintainers
- Problem: Local env differences (node/python versions)
  - Mitigation: include `.nvmrc`/`.python-version` and devcontainer config; provide Dockerfile for reproducible runs

Tiny example to include in quickstart (Python):

# example snippet (in README) - show minimal usage pattern (not real JSON in file)
# ---------------------------------
# pip install redwood-client==0.7.0
# export REDWOOD_API_KEY=test_demo_key
# python -c "from redwood_client import Client; c=Client(); print(c.text.generate('Hello world'))"
# ---------------------------------

Troubleshooting cheat sheet (short):
- If `make run-sample` fails with port-in-use: kill previous demo or run on `PORT=8081 make run-sample`
- If `npm ci` errors on node-gyp: ensure correct node version from `.nvmrc` or use Docker dev container
- If tests fail in CI but pass locally: check flaky test tag and re-run only fast-check workflow

Telemetry and experimental instrumentation (what to capture):
- Event: `dev:clone_repo` (anonymous, fires on `make run-sample` first-run)
- Event: `dev:run_sample_success` and `dev:run_sample_error` with durations
- Event: `dev:open_pr` (internal only) + `dev:pr_first_time` boolean
- Track time deltas for clone->run and clone->pr (for consenting internal devs)
- Log CI workflow durations for `fast-check` vs full test suite

Experiment plan (30-day pilot):
- Week 0: baseline metrics from GitHub + Slack (how many new contributors, time-to-first-PR)
- Week 1: land demo backend and Makefile targets across 3 repos (client-js, client-py, examples)
- Week 2: route contributor PRs through `fast-check` CI and measure PR turnaround
- Week 3: collect survey feedback from contributors (1-2 q: Was it easy? Where stuck?)
- Week 4: evaluate metrics and decide whether to expand to more repos or revert changes

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should demo-mode be enabled by default on main branch or only in `examples/`? (security tradeoff)
- How do we gate the `generate-test-token.sh` so external forks cannot misuse it?
- Which repos are in-scope for the pilot beyond client-py and client-js? (propose: examples, docs site repo)

Next actionable tasks (owner assignments):
- Maya: prototype `scripts/start-demo.sh` and `Makefile` skeleton (ETA: 2025-11-13)
- Evelyn: PR template update and GH Actions `fast-check` workflow draft (ETA: 2025-11-14)
- Samir: instrument `dev:*` telemetry events in `examples/` sample runner (ETA: 2025-11-17)
- Diego: coordinate with infra to add a small runner VM for demo-mode (internal only) (ETA: 2025-11-20)

Notes to self (style and tone):
- Keep prose short; prefer commands and checklists.
- Assume reader skims — put the single-command to run at the top of README.
- Do not rely on Console for first-pass developer experience.

References and related docs:
- Confluence: DEVEXP quickstarts (link above)
- Existing quickstarts: client-examples repo (internal)
- Slack thread: #dev-experience / thread TS-234 (search)

-- end of draft --
